approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from a bounded population of accepted high-scoring molecules. It uses score-quantile parent sampling, connected-fragment crossover and local graph mutations, including its retained formula-preserving aromatic nitrogen-position exchange. Stable identity admission checks each fresh candidate before a surplus pool is formed. A Gaussian process trained on all earlier accepted scores uses binary local-environment fingerprints to predict that pool, and correlated posterior draws choose the molecules submitted for evaluation. Accepted feedback updates both the breeding population and the full prediction archive.
approach.novelty: Make the posterior sensitive to how many times each local molecular environment occurs. Replace binary fingerprint presence with integer environment counts and the corresponding generalized Tanimoto covariance. Repeated ring or substituent environments can then change similarity even when their presence is already recorded. Earlier siblings changed survivor or parent allocation, graph edits and identity admission; they have not changed the posterior to retain environment multiplicity. This mechanism supplies quantitative representation to the existing learned selector. Its usefulness must be established through prospective prediction and the paired search results.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent n-9edaa26007c3 has complete supplied summaries and run logs with macro mean 0.5517706549878213 and population SD 0.008223094871288588, complete valid batches, and 593 strict best-generating-parent beats among 4350 evaluated offspring. Its molecular assessment documents repeated oversized aromatic assemblies and a very low-scoring repeated indole/amide product, alongside useful bounded families. The one targeted limitation is that its binary radius-two Morgan covariance erases the multiplicity of each hashed local environment. A read-only audit of its actual 4500 accepted trajectory occurrences using the same RDKit 2023.09.6 finds 4459 occurrences with a count bin greater than one, across 4296 of 4324 distinct identities; the maximum count is 46. The count-vector support exactly matches the inherited binary fingerprint for all 4324 identities. Applying the registered generalized count Tanimoto formula to its 6074 actual generating-parent/offspring pairs changes 6054 similarities by more than 1e-12. Mean count-minus-binary similarity is +0.17112610321684035, with range -0.2577205882352942 to +0.5624522171253823: counting changes metric weighting and supplies no uniform size penalty. The actual Parent prospective prediction MSE is 0.01697217317205435 against same-fit archive-mean MSE 0.03606287331064632; nominal mean plus/minus 1.96 logged latent SD contains 78.73563218390804 percent of accepted offspring scores. Only ten exact fingerprint-equivalent pool pairs occur across 435 pools, so exact tie removal is not the proposed explanation. The earlier selector node n-fc2c108a5253 and its Curate observation likewise establish useful average prediction with weak parent-beating yield and unresolved representation or exploration contributions. These measurements establish available multiplicity information and remaining predictive error; their causal connection to search quality remains untested.
hypothesis: Replace binary Morgan-presence covariance with generalized Tanimoto covariance on integer counts of the same hashed local molecular environments, so the accepted-feedback Gaussian process conditions on environment multiplicity.

finding_summary.headline: Environment counts change selection and lift mean score by 0.0226, but uncertainty coverage worsens
finding_summary.insights:
The useful change comes from reweighting ordinary similarity relationships, not from splitting exact fingerprint ties: the only binary-equivalent pair in the Child pools remained count-equivalent. Counts usually increased archive-to-pool similarity and reduced posterior uncertainty, but neither direction was universal. Their prediction advantage was much larger when passively applied to the Parent's selected stream than on their own selected stream, showing why historical prediction gains need to be checked after selection adapts. Sitagliptin supplies the largest score gain even though its paired MSE worsens and its latent intervals cover only one third of scored emissions. Improved mean prediction therefore does not fully explain the whole-search gain; the contribution of changed uncertainty to allocation remains open. Uncertainty calibration is now a concrete issue to probe separately.

The molecular assessment finds smaller families in several streams, yet oversized assemblies, unusual heteroatom bonds, constrained rings and unspecified stereochemistry remain. Counts preserve the same local environment vocabulary and many hashing collisions; they supply neither a demonstrated size penalty nor evidence of synthetic or geometric feasibility. These results establish count-sensitive posterior execution and utility on the supplied panel, while leaving broader chemical usefulness and transfer to other search distributions unresolved.
finding_summary.results:
Environment multiplicity changed the similarity matrices and posterior distribution in all 435 fits. On identical archives and pools, 69,570 of 69,600 predicted means changed; replaying the same random draws changed 434 of 435 selected batches. The three-seed macro mean rose from 0.55177 to 0.57434, a gain of 0.02257 above the registered 0.002 minimum. Two seed means improved and one fell. Mean final scores rose for sitagliptin by 0.06213, median similarity by 0.02333, DRD2 by 0.02056 and decoration hopping by 0.00911, while zaleplon fell by 0.00228. All evaluations completed; strict improvements over the best generating parent rose from 593 to 624 out of 4,350 offspring.

On the Child's identical scored molecules, the count model reduced prediction MSE from a passive binary model's 0.011797 to 0.011269, about 4.5%, and raised mean within-batch rank correlation from 0.469 to 0.550. The archive-mean baseline MSE was 0.042504. However, mean latent interval width shrank from 0.263 to 0.168, and nominal 95% coverage fell from 85.6% to 76.9%; including observation noise only raised count-model coverage to 77.2%. This is evidence for better average prediction and search outcomes on this panel, alongside worse uncertainty coverage.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich families become smaller in several streams, but unusual heteroatom bonds and unspecified ring stereochemistry persist
molecular.overall_character: All supplied tasks and their Parent trajectories were read. Each current task contains 900 records, including 870 optimizer proposals. Ring-closure text presence ranges from 0.9575 to 0.9851 and aromatic-text presence from 0.9517 to 0.9747; these are fractions of proposal strings containing the relevant syntax, not fractions of atoms. The products include indole carboxamides, linked nitrogen/oxygen heteroaromatics, aryl-bearing cyclic amines, medium-ring aza-dicarbonyl assemblies, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl heterocycles. Distinct families occur across seeds, while leading excerpts concentrate on related members within a family. Several streams are smaller on average than Parent n-9edaa26007c3, but small size does not remove N-F, N-S, unusual sulfur bonding, unsaturated small rings or difficult polycyclic connectivity. Every task has charged_rate and stereocentre_rate 0.0. Neutral strings still contain potentially basic amines; the strings do not establish solution or evaluator protonation states. Structural counts below are passive RDKit readings of the supplied trajectories, recorded in .slots/SPIRAL2.r0011-02-improve-L01.molecular-audit.json. Parsing establishes connectivity, without establishing a feasible conformation, stability or synthetic route.

per_task.generated_character: The main high-scoring family comprises medium-sized, heavily substituted indole carboxamides attached to phenyl or pyridyl rings. Methoxy or vinyl-ether groups, methyl/vinyl substituents, an indole NH and an amide carbonyl recur; many leading amides carry N-F or N-Cl. A conventional secondary-amide member has 24 heavy atoms and three rings. The highest observed molecule instead has a compact bridged nitrogen-containing core, a phenyl carboxamide with an N-S bond, and 24 heavy atoms. The indole/aryl amide components are familiar synthetic building blocks, whereas the N-halogen, N-sulfanyl and bridged variants are less routine endpoints. Mean proposal SMILES length is 42.2 versus Parent 44.7; halogen presence falls from the Parent digest 0.9609 to 0.623. The Parent highest observed record was an N-fluoro indole/pyridyl carboxamide at 0.46092619585962435. The current chemistry retains that broad family while increasing vinyl substitution and changing the leading bridged core.
liabilities: The leading N-F and N-Cl bonds are on amide nitrogen, rather than carbon-bound aromatic halogens; the highest molecule also has an N-S bond. These require separate chemical scrutiny from ordinary aryl carboxamides.
Vinyl ethers and the compact bridged nitrogen-containing core add reactivity or geometric questions. The bridged product has a potential stereochemical choice that its string does not specify.
missing_features: The low-end fragments lack the integrated fused-aromatic, carbonyl and aryl/heteroaryl arrangement expressed by the stronger molecules; some late substitutions also fail to retain its favorable balance.

Conventional amide substitution is demonstrated near the leading scores, but an equally strong family with both ordinary bond chemistry and straightforward alternative core connectivity is not established. The observations do not identify an unseen target-specific group that must be added.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxy indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145. The cited divinyl/methoxy pyridyl secondary amide scores 0.4330127018922193; replacing its amide hydrogen with either Cl or F gives 0.4423126980074005 in both cases. The N-fluoro phenyl/vinyl-ether congener reaches 0.4484138510190879, and the bridged N-S-containing product reaches 0.45766047024715. Methane scores 0.0. A late amino-substituted indole congener scores 0.2859212949869023 despite retaining the amide and aromatic rings. The visible gradient favors a particular combined aromatic/carbonyl/substituent arrangement over fragments, and tolerates unusual amide substitution; it does not show a general benefit from adding nitrogen or halogen.

per_task.generated_character: The leading excerpt contains a fused nitrogen/oxygen carbonyl heteroaromatic core connected through an aryl ether to pyridyl rings, including a nitrile-bearing terminal ring. Methoxy and methyl groups accompany branched polyenes bearing carbon-bound F, Cl and Br. The first cited product has 43 heavy atoms and four perceived rings; a longer equally scoring congener has 50 heavy atoms with the same ring count. The digest final seed-2 tail belongs to a different, smaller family of partially saturated fused diaza rings, arylamino methoxy-bearing carbon centres and substituted pyridines. Seed 0 still explores much larger repeated heteroaromatic assemblies. Mean proposal SMILES length is 94.6 versus Parent 125.3, but the maximum is 266 versus Parent 237. Ring and aromatic text presence are both 0.9713. Familiar heteroaryl and ether components coexist with dense substitution, unsaturated chains and difficult complete structures.
liabilities: Long branched polyenes with several carbon-bound halogens add synthetic and geometric complexity without a corresponding score separation in the cited plateau.

The smaller final family contains N,O-acetal-like carbon centres and, in the cited strong final product, an N-O linkage. Its alternative bond chemistry is not automatically resolved by its smaller size.
The multiple substituted alkenes and saturated stereogenic centres have no specified configurations in the emitted strings.
missing_features: The small fragments and truncated bis-pyridyl product lack the richer connected core/substituent arrangement visible in the stronger products.

The leading excerpt underrepresents compact, conventionally substituted alternatives that retain the useful connected heteroaromatic pattern without polyene extension. Near-equal scores for expanded appendages do not identify a missing decoration or support unlimited growth.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Chloroacetylene and other small fragments sit at 0.5, while the initial aryl dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.548381482770623. The late bis-pyridyl hydrazine scores 0.5557275541795665, compared with 0.6109149100540779 for a larger connected diaza/aryl-amino-ether product. The leading polyene/heteroaromatic structure and its longer brominated congeners all receive 0.6199818405862896; duplicating more of the unsaturated appendage gives 0.619706525936414. Thus connected aromatic and heteroatom patterns distinguish the stronger molecules, but substantial peripheral growth is nearly score-neutral here. A carbonyl is present in the leading family and absent from a strong late family, so no mandatory carbonyl requirement follows. The Parent highest observed record was a much larger repeated assembly at 0.6114128757484105; the current higher observed maximum is associated with a smaller core assembly, without eliminating the oversized tail.

per_task.generated_character: The highest product is a medium-sized N-propyl pyrrolidine joined through a fluorinated carbon to a rigid oxygen-containing polycycle bearing aromatic and pyridyl surfaces. It has 26 heavy atoms and several substituted saturated centres. Other leaders combine an aminoethyl-substituted pyrrolidine with a biaryl/oxygen-ring framework. A separate high-scoring family is more flexible: a tertiary aminoalkyl chain connects substituted aromatic rings through a sulfur centre drawn with simultaneous S=C and S=O bonds; aryl halogens and thioether or O-S appendages occur. The final seed-2 family includes aryl-linked saturated diaza rings and phenolic/cyclic ether functionality. Mean proposal SMILES length is 56.2 versus Parent 65.1; ring presence is 0.9736, aromatic presence 0.9655 and halogen presence 0.9885. Recognizable aryl/basic-amine chemistry is abundant, alongside more questionable sulfur, peroxide and polycyclic endpoints.
liabilities: The S=C/S=O centre, O-S substituents and the final O-O bridge are unusual chemical contexts whose accepted scores do not establish stability or a practical synthetic route.
Substituted pyrrolidine, fluorinated connector and polycyclic centres create stereochemical and conformational choices left unresolved by the submitted connectivity.
Almost all proposals contain halogens by the digest text counter. This includes conventional carbon-halogen bonds and does not by itself establish useful physical properties.
missing_features: The weak sulfonylated and truncated examples do not retain the same accessible amine character and connected aromatic arrangement as the leaders. This is a functional-context gap, not a shortage of nitrogen atoms.

The strongest saturated and polycyclic products leave their stereochemical alternatives unspecified. Explicit charge-state alternatives are also absent from the strings, although evaluator protonation handling and any benefit from alternative states are not established here.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The rigid N-propyl pyrrolidine product scores 0.9964552366323939, the aminoethyl pyrrolidine/biaryl product 0.9959112136066024, and the flexible sulfur-containing tertiary amine 0.9959491085611949. In a close propyl-substituted biaryl pair, removing the fluorine from the connecting saturated carbon changes 0.9953366403155401 to 0.9949585989164051, leaving both high. The low N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine/ketone scores 0.00021169315013374197; its ring nitrogen is chemically different from an unacylated tertiary amine, and its connected aromatic surface also differs. A small aryl hydroperoxide scores 0.001441121247095158. A late aryl/diaza-ring product with an aldehyde scores 0.9782609553322966, while the differently connected bridged peroxide tail product scores 0.6566255585773542. Together these observations favor the combined aryl/amine/connecting-geometry arrangement, while neither a particular fluorine nor a single rigid topology is essential in the shown set. The Parent highest observed record, 0.9914038363125457, belonged to another aryl/diaza-amine family; the current products change topology while retaining the broad amine/aromatic theme.

per_task.generated_character: The leading products are medium-to-large aza-dicarbonyl ring assemblies joining propyl- and ethoxy-substituted aromatic rings through a diaryl ether and additional saturated or unsaturated nitrogen/carbon connections. N-methyl lactam-like carbonyl environments recur; the highest product also contains an N-N ring-junction bond. It has 33 heavy atoms and perceived rings of sizes 6, 6, 7 and 10. Closely related products move the nitrogen connection or contract/expand the larger ring. The final seed-2 products instead attach a quinoline-like aromatic unit to annulated nitrogen-containing dicarbonyl rings. Mean SMILES length is 55.4 versus Parent 56.2; ring presence is 0.9851, aromatic presence 0.9747 and halogen presence only 0.1356. This is substantial saturated and aromatic ring chemistry, but the complete interconnected medium-ring systems would require deliberate synthetic and stereochemical planning.
liabilities: Interconnected medium rings, N-N linkages and changing amine versus lactam environments make the whole structures more challenging than their familiar isolated carbonyl and aryl groups suggest.
The saturated ring junctions and substituted carbon centres have no specified stereochemistry; ring closure in SMILES is not a conformation or synthesis demonstration.
missing_features: The low fragments lack the combined aromatic surfaces and nitrogen/carbonyl arrangement represented by the stronger connected molecules.

The leading excerpt lacks evidence for straightforward alternative ring connections that retain this arrangement with established stereochemistry and geometric feasibility. No particular unseen scaffold or extra nitrogen can be inferred from the observed near-ties.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.1678386594791329. The leading diaryl-ether/aza-dicarbonyl assembly scores 0.24321515648721753, while its ring-contracted NH-linked relative scores 0.2382582318459322. A closely related NH-linked member and its carbon-for-nitrogen analogue both score 0.23652880504920906; adding aryl fluorine to the leading framework gives 0.23732594613885244. The final quinoline/aza-dicarbonyl product scores 0.23035161967494103, whereas the cited small SBr fragment scores 0.0. The gradient supports an integrated aromatic, cyclic nitrogen and dicarbonyl arrangement, with sensitivity to their connections; these examples do not support indiscriminate nitrogen addition or halogenation. The Parent highest observed record was a different complex aza-dicarbonyl ring assembly at 0.21361011906838706. The higher current maximum accompanies changed medium-ring connectivity, without evidence of simpler leading chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family links a methoxyphenyl ring to a fused nitrogen-rich heterocycle carrying a carbonyl and an exocyclic imino group. It also bears a fluorinated four- or five-member partially unsaturated nitrogen ring; direct N-F bonds and N-fluoromethyl substitution recur on the fused core. The highest product has 27 heavy atoms and a four-member unsaturated aza ring, with an unassigned substituted saturated centre. The final seed-2 tail is mainly a smaller phenol-linked carbonyl/imino heterocyclic family bearing fluoroalkyl groups; it also includes a tiny OBr proposal. Mean SMILES length falls from Parent 53.9 to 47.3. Cumulated-double-bond text presence falls from Parent 0.2218 to 0.0046, while current halogen presence remains 0.8954 and ring presence 0.9575. The Parent short arene bridges and cyclic-cumulene family are replaced in the leading excerpt by different small-ring and N-fluorination liabilities, rather than clearly conventional medicinal products.
liabilities: Direct N-F bonds on carbonyl/imino ring nitrogens are chemically different from carbon-bound fluorine and are prominent even among the highest scores.

The four-member unsaturated nitrogen ring concentrates substitution and imposes ring-geometry constraints. Its higher score than the closely related five-member ring does not validate its stability, geometry or synthesis.
Exocyclic imino functionality introduces tautomeric possibilities, and the fluorinated small-ring attachment centre has no assigned configuration.
missing_features: The tiny proposals and the repeated large assembly lack the bounded connected feature balance expressed by the stronger products; simply adding more of the same heterocycle does not retain it.

The highest excerpt does not demonstrate a version combining the useful polar and fluorinated features with ordinary substituent bonding, demonstrated ring feasibility and specified stereochemistry. It cannot establish which unseen pharmacophore or stereoisomer would improve the objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.0020944534688323298. The leading carbonyl/imino product with a four-member unsaturated nitrogen ring scores 0.6510211907030741; inserting a methylene into that ring while retaining the other shown substituents gives the cited five-member analogue at 0.6151435340472637. Within another five-member-ring pair, replacing one direct N-F substituent by N-CH2F changes 0.6492585029324071 to 0.623934455699338. Thus the score tolerates and sometimes favors the chemically less routine local contexts in these comparisons. The final phenol/fluoroalkyl product scores 0.5136226132583438, while a different hydroxycyclobutenyl-substituted core scores 0.056329114721316687. The large repeated heterocyclic assembly scores 5.038398954372863e-25 and the tiny F proposal 1.1043196211273875e-26. Bounded size and the connected aromatic/polar/fluorinated arrangement matter in the visible series; no single group requirement follows from these multiple families. The Parent highest observed record was an amino/fluoro bridged-arene dicarbonyl product at 0.5750908973498792. The current higher maximum is associated with a different compact imino/small-aza-ring family.

transferable_gaps.evidence: C=Cc1cc2[nH]c(C(=O)Nc3cccnc3)cc2c(OC)c1C=C scores 0.4330127018922193, while its N-fluoro and N-chloro analogues both score 0.4423126980074005. C=S(=O)(CN(CCC)CCC(CC)c1cc(Br)cc(SC)c1)c1ccc(N)cc1Cl scores 0.9959491085611949 with simultaneous sulfur-carbon and sulfur-oxygen double bonds. These actual high-scoring outputs show that feedback can retain unusual local chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional functional-group bonding when decorating otherwise recognizable molecular cores.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make chemically coherent alternatives available that distinguish functional-group roles and attachment atoms, including ordinary amide and carbon-bound substituent contexts. Preserve the capacity to compare alternatives through available feedback without treating element presence or valence acceptance as evidence of equivalent chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: COc1ccccc1-n1cc2c(c1C1(F)C=CN1)c(=O)n(CF)c(=N)n2F contains a four-member unsaturated aza ring and scores 0.6510211907030741; the cited methylene-expanded analogue scores 0.6151435340472637. CCCc1ccc2c(c1)CN1C(CCc3c(OCC)cccc3O2)C(=O)N(C)CC(=O)N1C contains interconnected medium-ring and diaryl-ether connectivity. Compact size and a high ring-text rate do not resolve these geometry questions.
transferable_gaps.gap: The emitted ring chemistry does not demonstrate consistent control of spatially credible topology and accessible ring connections.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support ring construction and rearrangement that account for ring size, bridge attachment geometry, multiple-bond placement and chemically credible closure alternatives. This should expose different topologies with comparable functional roles; the observations do not justify globally favoring or forbidding one ring size.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task digest has stereocentre_rate 0.0. CCCN1CCCC1C(F)C1Oc2c3ccc1c2Cc1c(Cl)ccnc1-3 has substituted pyrrolidine, connector and polycyclic centres, and COc1ccccc1-n1cc2c(c1C1(F)C=CN1)c(=O)n(CF)c(=N)n2F has a substituted fluorinated small-ring centre. Neither emitted string assigns the corresponding configurations; the branched polyene family also leaves its alkene geometry unspecified.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator leaves stereochemical choices unspecified in the saturated, bridged and fluorinated structures it emits.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve existing stereochemical information and make consistent configuration choices available when structural edits create or change stereogenic centres or double bonds. Distinguish resulting isomers in molecular identity while leaving their usefulness to the available feedback; no preferred isomer is inferred from these connectivity-only observations.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One proposal stream has mean SMILES length 94.6 and maximum 266, compared with its Parent mean 125.3 and maximum 237. Its leading polyene/heteroaromatic assembly and substantially elongated congeners all score 0.6199818405862896. Elsewhere, CCc1ccc(O)c(-n2c(CC)c3c(=O)n(-n4c(=O)n(C)c(=N)c5c(CC)n(-c6cc(CC)ccc6O)c(F)c54)c(=O)n(C)c3c2F)c1 scores 5.038398954372863e-25, while late tiny fragments also persist. Reduced average size therefore coexists with both repeated growth and loss of the useful connected structure.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not consistently maintain coherent molecular scale and connected functional features during structural variation.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expose edits that change core connectivity or substituent placement while retaining a coherent set of connected functional features, and allow redundant appendages to be simplified. Use general chemical structure and observed feedback to compare these alternatives; avoid a formula, size target or preferred scaffold keyed to an objective.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

retained_mechanisms: Task-local scored molecular-graph population with score-ranked parent sampling across three high-ranked quantiles
Local atom/bond mutation, inner retries and occasional multi-step graph walks
Direct formula-preserving same-six-member-aromatic-ring C/N positional exchange in the inherited per-site replacement menu, including its invariant gates and passive mutation-sequence receipts
Chemical sanitization, stable canonical/isomeric identity admission with graph-equivalent alias confirmation, novelty rejection and bounded graph-based retries for complete pools
Bounded greedy score-ranked survival and subsequent breeding from accepted offspring
Accepted-only task-local Gaussian-process archive with full ordered accepted history, archive-mean centering, population-SD scaling and fixed observation noise
Integer-count Morgan environment representation in the inherited hashed radius-two vocabulary, generalized squared-norm Tanimoto covariance, and consistent pool/next-fit conditional predictions

Exact joint posterior sampling over fresh offspring pools, masked batch selection and accepted-feedback refitting; first-jitter factorization succeeds throughout and numerical fallback remains retained but unexercised
